I am writing this email with great disappointment and concern regarding my Maruti Baleno Delta (Registration No. PB-27N-0681), purchased in February 2026. I also escalated the matter to the Regional Service Manager, Mr. Sandip Nikam.

Only after my intervention was the vehicle dismantled and inspected. I was then shown a burnt clutch plate and informed that the failure was due to my driving habits. I respectfully disagree with this conclusion, as I have been driving manual transmission vehicles for more than 15 years without experiencing such a failure. A clutch plate failure at merely 4,003 kilometers is highly unusual and raises serious concerns regarding product quality, manufacturing standards, component quality, or technical assessment procedures.

Since the vehicle was extremely new and remained under warranty, I requested goodwill support. The service center agreed to provide a 35% waiver on parts. However, shortly thereafter, I was informed that the required clutch plate and flywheel were not available in the Maruti warehouse and were reportedly unavailable across the entire North Zone. I was further informed that a Back Order Request (BOR) had been raised.

On 20 June 2026, after another visit to the workshop, I was informed that the parts were still unavailable and that several customer orders placed before mine were also pending due to non-availability of stock.

During this period, I raised multiple complaints with Maruti Suzuki Customer Care (contact@maruti.co.in), spoke with the Territory Service Manager Mr. Srijan Dwivedi, and repeatedly followed up with Regional Service Manager Mr. Sandip Nikam. Despite these efforts, no definite resolution timeline has been provided. I also requested an opportunity to discuss the matter with the General Manager of CM Auto Sales, Mr. Vaibhav Mahajan,( through service center manager) but my request was declined.

Today, my vehicle has remained immobilized at the service center for nine days solely because genuine Maruti spare parts are unavailable.

This situation is particularly concerning because Maruti Suzuki strongly advises and threatened customers to use only genuine parts to maintain warranty coverage. Yet, when a genuine part is required, the company is unable to supply it within a reasonable timeframe. Such a situation is unacceptable for a leading automobile manufacturer and has caused significant inconvenience, financial loss, and mental stress.

As a customer who purchased a new Maruti vehicle based on the company's reputation for reliability, service support, and spare parts availability, I am deeply disappointed. The premature failure of critical components, coupled with the inability to provide timely repairs, has completely eroded my trust and confidence in the vehicle and the brand.

• Non-availability of standard spare parts.
• Prolonged vehicle downtime.
• Lack of a committed repair timeline.
• Significant inconvenience and loss of confidence in the product.

description: Customer VOC:I wish to lodge a formal complaint against Daga Motors regarding the purchase process of a new Maruti Suzuki Alto K10 and the handling of my old vehicle under the scrappage scheme. On 8 May 2026, I visited Daga Motors to purchase a new Alto K10. I informed the sales executive that my existing vehicle was a 2015 Tata Indigo registered as a commercial vehicle and that I intended to purchase the new Alto K10 as a private vehicle. The executive assured me that the scrappage benefits would still be applicable. The deal offered to me was as follows: 1. Alto K10 On-Road Price: ₹4,50,000 2. Consumer Bonus: ₹25,000 3. Scrap Value of Old Vehicle: ₹20,000 4. Additional Exchange/Scrappage Bonus: ₹25,000 on submission of the scrappage certificate Based on these assurances, I paid a booking amount of ₹2,100 on 10 May 2026. I would also like to highlight that the sales executive displayed very limited product knowledge and was unable to explain even basic vehicle specifications. Most of the vehicle-related information had to be obtained by me independently. Thereafter, the loan process was initiated. Throughout the process, I personally coordinated with the loan provider, submitted documents, and followed up on approvals, while the showroom staff provided minimal support. On 13 May 2026, the loan provider informed me that although I had applied for a loan of ₹3,70,000, only ₹3,00,000 had been approved. I agreed to arrange the remaining amount myself. After receiving confirmation regarding the loan, I instructed Daga Motors to collect my old Tata Indigo from the mechanic workshop for scrapping. The vehicle was taken on 14 May 2026 and subsequently scrapped. However, the scrap value of ₹20,000 was not credited to my account and was instead retained by the showroom. On 16 May 2026, when I visited the showroom to take delivery of the vehicle, I was informed that my loan could not proceed because my mother's details had been added as nominee and that I must provide my father's documents. During my very first visit, I had clearly informed the showroom that my father was separated from the family and that obtaining his documents would be difficult. Despite this, the showroom insisted that adding my father was mandatory and stated that it was a bank requirement. After considerable effort, I arranged my father's documents. However, during verification, he did not provide consent, resulting in loan rejection. Following this, Daga Motors submitted my application to multiple banks. Due to repeated loan inquiries and rejections, my CIBIL score dropped from approximately 750 to 695. Eventually, I was informed that no bank was willing to approve my loan and that I should either arrange the entire amount in cash or cancel the purchase. Subsequently, I approached Kamthi Motors, Chhindwara, where the same vehicle was offered to me. They successfully arranged a loan of ₹3,70,000 through a local bank. However, they informed me that the additional ₹25,000 scrappage/exchange bonus was not applicable because my old vehicle was commercial while the new vehicle was being purchased as a private vehicle. They further informed me that Daga Motors had provided incorrect information regarding eligibility for this benefit. As my old vehicle had already been scrapped by Daga Motors and I had no alternative, I proceeded with the purchase of the Alto K10 from Kamthi Motors on 15 June 2026 without receiving the ₹25,000 scrappage/exchange bonus. When I contacted Daga Motors regarding this issue, they initially stated that the bonus could still be claimed. However, when I requested them to coordinate with Kamthi Motors, they stopped responding to my calls. Thereafter, I visited Daga Motors to obtain a refund of my booking amount. Out of the ₹2,100 booking amount, only ₹1,600 was refunded, and ₹500 was deducted without any proper explanation. When I requested payment of the ₹20,000 scrap value of my old vehicle, I was told to wait another 10 days. Most importantly, Daga Motors later informed me that the scrappage certificate was applicable only for the purchase of a commercial vehicle and not for a private vehicle. This directly contradicts the assurances given to me before they collected and scrapped my old vehicle. Had I been informed correctly from the beginning, I would never have allowed my vehicle to be scrapped through them. I request Maruti Suzuki to investigate the matter and provide appropriate resolution. Specifically, I seek: 1. Immediate release/payment of the ₹20,000 scrap value of my old Tata Indigo 2. Clarification regarding the eligibility of the ₹25,000 scrappage/exchange bonus and accountability for the incorrect information provided by Daga Motors. 3. Explanation for the unauthorized deduction of ₹500 from my booking amount. 4. Investigation into the conduct of the dealership staff and the deficient handling of my loan application. 5. Appropriate compensation and corrective action for the financial loss, inconvenience, and adverse impact on my CIBIL score caused by the dealership's actions.=====synopsis==========The customer's concernregarding severe misrepresentation and mismanagement during the purchase process of a new Maruti Suzuki Alto K10 and the handling of his old commercial vehicle under the scrappage scheme. After being forced to complete the purchase through Kamthi Motors—where he discovered that the ₹25,000 bonus was legally invalid for his vehicle type—the complainant was left with a financial deficit, an unexplained ₹500 deduction from his refunded booking amount, and an uncooperative response from Daga Motors. Consequently, he requests Maruti Suzuki's urgent intervention to secure the immediate release of his ₹20,000 scrap value, a refund of the unauthorized ₹500 deduction, official clarification on scrappage eligibility, a formal investigation into the dealership's negligent staff, and appropriate compensation for his financial loss, inconvenience, and credit damage.
